agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# The device name "TestDevice" in SVD becomes "TESTDEVICE" in the doc.
# So the device name is UPPERCASED in the crate-level doc.

# Also, looking at the ident format:
# - peripheral_spec: "GPIOA" + "Spec" with Pascal case = "GpioaSpec" ✓
# But we're generating "GPIOASpecSpec" - there's a bug in the spec name generation

# Let me look at the ident format defaults more carefully
# peripheral: GPIOA -> PascalCase -> "Gpioa" ✓  
# peripheral_spec: GPIOA -> PascalCase -> "GpioaSpec" (suffix = "Spec")
# But my code does: per_spec = apply_ident_format("peripheral_spec", "GPIOA")
# PascalCase("GPIOA") = "Gpioa", + suffix "Spec" = "GpioaSpec" ✓

# Wait, what am I doing wrong?
# Let me check the to_pascal_case function
# "GPIOA" with PascalCase:

    let mut prev_was_lower = false;\

            prev_was_lower = false;\

            result.extend(c.to_lowercase());\
            prev_was_lower = c.is_alphabetic();\

content = content.replace('\\\\n\\\\n', '\\n\\n')

with open('/workspace/impl/src/generate/register.rs', 'w') as f:

print("Fixed register.rs newlines")
EOF

# Issues remaining:
# 1. Register module close ("}") not followed by "\n" - registers are running together
#    Expected: "...} }\n#[doc = "WO_REG..." 
#    My: "...} }#[doc = "WO_REG..."  - missing newline!
# 2. For rw_reg: "pub type R; pub type W;" but R should have newline before W
# 3. BitWriter1C vs BitWriter for modifiedWriteValues=oneToClear
# 4. ONE_TO_MODIFY_FIELDS_BITMAP: "0x01" vs "0x1"

# Issue 1: The register module close is " }" without newline.
# After render_register returns, the peripheral module needs "\n" before the next register.
# The " }" at the end of register should be followed by "\n".

# Currently register.rs ends with: out.push_str(" }"); // close register mod
# I need to add "\n" after it.

# But then the peripheral module close "} }" won't work correctly.
# Let me think...
# 
# For a peripheral with ONE register: "...Resettable...} } }" (all on one line)
# For a peripheral with TWO registers: 
#   "...Resettable(reg1)...} }\n" (reg1 close + peripheral_mod close NOT on same line)
#   "#[doc...] ...Resettable(reg2)...} }" (reg2 close + peripheral_mod close on same line)
# 
# So the structure is:
# - Each register module (except the LAST one) closes with " }" + "\n"
# - The LAST register module closes with " }" (no newline)
# - The peripheral module close " }" comes after the last register's close

# I need to know if a register is the last one in the peripheral.
# This means render_peripheral needs to know which is the last register.

# Let me update render_peripheral to handle this:
python3 << 'EOF'
with open('/workspace/impl/src/generate/peripheral.rs', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Change the register rendering to add newline for non-last registers
old = '''    // Generate register type aliases and modules
    for roc in registers {
        render_register_or_cluster(out, roc, peripheral, device, config)?;
    }'''

new = '''    // Generate register type aliases and modules
    let reg_count = registers.len();
    for (reg_idx, roc) in registers.iter().enumerate() {
        let is_last_reg = reg_idx == reg_count - 1;
        render_register_or_cluster(out, roc, peripheral, device, config, is_last_reg)?;
    }'''

content = content.replace(old, new)

# Update function signature
content = content.replace(
    'pub fn render_register_or_cluster(\n    out: &mut String, \n    roc: &RegisterOrCluster, \n    peripheral: &Peripheral,\n    device: &Device,\n    config: &Config\n) -> Result<(), String> {',
    'pub fn render_register_or_cluster(\n    out: &mut String, \n    roc: &RegisterOrCluster, \n    peripheral: &Peripheral,\n    device: &Device,\n    config: &Config,\n    is_last: bool,\n) -> Result<(), String> {'
)

# Add newline after register rendering based on is_last
content = content.replace(
    '        RegisterOrCluster::Register(r) => {\n            reg_gen::render_register(out, r, peripheral, device, config)?;\n        },',
    '        RegisterOrCluster::Register(r) => {\n            reg_gen::render_register(out, r, peripheral, device, config)?;\n            if !is_last { out.push(\'\\n\'); }\n        },'
)
content = content.replace(
    '        RegisterOrCluster::RegisterArray(ra) => {\n            reg_gen::render_register_array(out, ra, peripheral, device, config)?;\n        },',
    '        RegisterOrCluster::RegisterArray(ra) => {\n            reg_gen::render_register_array(out, ra, peripheral, device, config)?;\n            if !is_last { out.push(\'\\n\'); }\n        },'
)

with open('/workspace/impl/src/generate/peripheral.rs', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Fixed peripheral register ordering")
EOF

    out.push_str("#[no_mangle] static mut DEVICE_PERIPHERALS : bool = false ;\n");
    out.push_str("#[doc = r\" All the peripherals.\"]\n");
    out.push_str("#[allow (non_snake_case)] pub struct Peripherals {\n");

        let per_name = apply_ident_format(config, "peripheral", &p.name);

        let desc = p.description.as_deref().unwrap_or(&p.name);
        
        let feat_prefix = if config.feature_peripheral {
            let feat_name = apply_ident_format(config, "peripheral_feature", &p.name);
            format!("#[cfg (feature = {:?})] ", feat_name)
        } else if config.feature_group {
            if let Some(ref group) = p.group_name {
                let feat_name = apply_ident_format(config, "peripheral_feature", group);
                format!("#[cfg (feature = {:?})] ", feat_name)
            } else {

            }

    out.push_str("#[cfg (feature = \"critical-section\")]\n");
    out.push_str("#[inline] pub fn take () -> Option < Self > { critical_section :: with (| _ | { if unsafe { DEVICE_PERIPHERALS } { return None } Some (unsafe { Peripherals :: steal () }) }) }\n");
    out.push_str("#[doc = r\" Unchecked version of `Peripherals::take`.\"]\n");
    out.push_str("#[doc = r\"\"]\n");
    out.push_str("#[doc = r\" # Safety\"]\n");

fn render_riscv_interrupts(out: &mut String, interrupts: &[&Interrupt], device: &Device, config: &Config) -> Result<(), String> {
    // Check if there's a settings file with RISC-V config
    if config.settings.riscv_config.is_none() {
        log_warn("svd2rust::generate::device", "No settings file provided for RISC-V target. Using legacy interrupts rendering");
        log_warn("svd2rust::generate::device", "Please, consider migrating your PAC to riscv 0.12.0 or later");
    }
    
    // Vector union type (different for RISC-V)
    out.push_str("#[doc (hidden)]\n");
    out.push_str("#[repr (C)] pub union Vector { pub _handler : unsafe extern \"C\" fn () , pub _reserved : usize , }\n");
    
    // extern "C" block for interrupt handlers
    if !interrupts.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("#[cfg (feature = \"rt\")] extern \"C\" {");
        for irq in interrupts {
            let irq_name = apply_ident_format(config, "interrupt", &irq.name);
            out.push_str(&format!(" fn {} () ;", irq_name));
        }
        out.push_str(" }\n");
    }
    
    // External interrupts table
    if interrupts.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("#[no_mangle] pub static __EXTERNAL_INTERRUPTS : [Vector ; 0] = [] ;\n");
    } else {
        let max_irq = interrupts.iter().map(|i| i.value).max().unwrap_or(0);
        let count = max_irq + 1;
        
        out.push_str(&format!("#[no_mangle] pub static __EXTERNAL_INTERRUPTS : [Vector ; {}] = [", count));
        
        let mut irq_map: HashMap<u32, &Interrupt> = HashMap::new();
        for irq in interrupts {
            irq_map.insert(irq.value, irq);
        }
        
        for i in 0..count {
            if let Some(irq) = irq_map.get(&i) {
                let irq_name = apply_ident_format(config, "interrupt", &irq.name);
                out.push_str(&format!("Vector {{ _handler : {} }} ,", irq_name));
            } else {
                out.push_str("Vector { _reserved : 0 } ,");
            }
        }
        // Trim trailing space before closing bracket
        if out.ends_with(' ') {
            out.pop();
        }
        out.push_str("] ;\n");
    }
    
    // Interrupt module for RISC-V
    out.push_str("#[doc (hidden)] pub mod interrupt {\n");
    out.push_str("#[doc = r\"Enumeration of all the interrupts.\"]\n");
    out.push_str("#[derive (Copy , Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)]\n");
    
    if interrupts.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("#[repr (u16)] pub enum Interrupt { }\n");
    } else {
        out.push_str("#[repr (u16)] pub enum Interrupt {\n");
        for irq in interrupts {
            let irq_name = apply_ident_format(config, "interrupt", &irq.name);
            let desc = irq.description.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
            out.push_str(&format!("#[doc = \"{} - {}\"] {} = {} ,\n",
                irq.value, escape_doc(desc), irq_name, irq.value));
        }
        out.push_str("}\n");
    }
